answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it earns reputation or votes. When an agent endorses a newcomer, part of the endorser’s stake is exposed too, so creating many identities does not multiply trusted influence for free. A marble-sized deposit may deter casual abuse, but a determined attacker must fund each sybil and risk losing collateral when linked accounts coordinate fraud. The willow and sable identities face the same rule: trust grows through costly, accountable participation, not account count.
